leaves.name: bShStandardModel
leaves.doc: r16-thm1 (round 2), kept in r16-thm1b: the bridge B-Sh. Shimura's standard model of X_1(N) over Q with its Q-rational Hecke correspondences xi_p and diamond operators <d> is the kernel's model: for every X with IsX1Gen, a rational point and Jacobian J, there are endomorphisms T_p, <d> of J over Q acting on classes of the points x_tau by the double-coset formulas IsHeckeT, IsDiamond (pinned by AfTateLam.HeckePin). Same statement as AfTateLam.HeckeJ1DS (heckeJ1DS_of_bSh). Split (r16-thm1b section 3): (B2) rationality of the Hecke ring over Q on Shimura's model is printed in Shimura 1973 p. 526 (AI page read, no citation on the page); (B3) a Q-rational correspondence induces an endomorphism of J over Q (standard); left ON THE SPOT: (B1) the kernel's IsX1Gen model is Shimura's standard model (defined in Shimura 1971, which the 1973 print cites) and (B4) Shimura's xi_p, <d> act on the classes of the x_tau by DS's double-coset formulas (convention dictionary).
leaves.flag: pending review: bridge B-Sh; rationality of the Hecke ring over Q printed in Shimura 1973 p. 526 (AI page read, no citation on the page); ON THE SPOT: the kernel's IsX1Gen model is Shimura's standard model (defined by citation of Shimura 1971) and xi_p, <d> act by DS's double-coset formulas (convention dictionary)
leaves.source: Shimura, J. Math. Soc. Japan 25 (1973), 523-544, p. 526 (rationality of the Hecke ring; AI page read); the model and the double-coset dictionary are not printed there (Shimura 1971, cited by the 1973 print for its standard model)

leaves.name: shimuraThm1Af
leaves.doc:
r16-thm1b: Shimura 1973 Thm 1 as printed, one row. For a newform f in S_2(Gamma_1(N)) with nebentypus chi, the kernel's model X of X_1(N), Jacobian J, Hecke operators T_p = xi_p, : K_f finite over Q, and there is a triple (A, nu, theta) with Shimura's clauses (i) nu surjective with connected kernel, (ii) nu o xi_n = theta(a_n) o nu at n = p and n = p^2 (xi_{p^2} = T_p^2 - p

), (iii) dim A = [K_f : Q], and IsAfQuotient (ker nu = I_f J: nu kills I_f J and is universal for that), unique up to a nu-compatible isomorphism over Q among triples with (i)-(iii). Printed (AI page read): C = Ker(nu) (p. 525), C from the ideal annihilating f intersected with End(J) (p. 526), uniqueness up to isomorphisms over Q (p. 526), dimension and tangent space from m = 1 via q-expansions (p. 527). ON THE SPOT steps: C = I_f J (the ideal is ker rho, saturation, Hecke relations in both directions); (ii) for all n from p and p^2 via xi_{p^2} = T_p^2 - p

(a theorem step, the Hecke relation); nu-compatible isomorphisms. Euler clause and (iv) not in this row.
leaves.flag:
pending review: Shimura 1973 Thm 1 as printed (AI page read: Ker nu p. 525, uniqueness up to isomorphisms over Q p. 526, tangent space and m = 1 from q-expansions p. 527, C from the ideal intersected with End(J) p. 526); on-the-spot steps: C = I_f J (the ideal is ker rho, saturation, Hecke relations in both directions), (ii) for all n from p and p^2 via xi_{p^2} = T_p^2 - p

(theorem step), nu-compatible isomorphisms; misprint in the f_sigma sentence before (iv) on p. 526 ('f_sigma | T_n = a_n^sigma f' for 'a_n^sigma f_sigma') recorded in docs/research/r16-thm1b.md
leaves.source: Shimura, On the factors of the jacobian variety of a modular function field, J. Math. Soc. Japan 25 (1973), 523-544, Theorem 1 and its construction (pp. 525-527; AI page read); cited by diophantine_zq.tex (shimura-factors)
